Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015) developed the 10-item Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) — an updated and refined version of the BAS. Here, we examined the psychometric properties of BAS-2 scores in Poland for several reasons.

Correlation between body appreciation an.evidence_source: In terms of convergent validity, we predicted that Polish BAS-2 scores would be significantly and negatively correlated with scores on measures of well-being (self-esteem, positive affect, and positive orientation) and negatively correlated with body mass index (BMI), as demonstrated by previous validations of the scale (Alleva et al., 2016; Atari, 2016; Swami et al., 2017; Swami & Ng, 2015; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015).
Correlation between body appreciation an.warning: The text only states a prediction for the correlation, not an actual reported value from the study's results.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section discusses the concept of positive body image and body appreciation, detailing the development and validation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its updated version, the BAS-2. It reviews previous cross-cultural studies on these scales and then outlines the rationale and predictions for the current study, which aims to examine the psychometric properties of BAS-2 scores in Poland, including its factor structure, invariance across sex, and correlations with well-being measures and BMI. The text implies a single study (Study X) is being conducted.
